rust.summary:
P3 is done. Every settle command passes, and so do cargo fmt, clippy (default lane and internals lane) and the openpyxl exchange. Nothing was committed.

**Number formats (`excel/format.rs`, new)**
- `FormatCode` has `from_code`, `builtin`, `general`, `is_general`, `kind`, `render`, `with_decimals` and `code`, plus `Display`, `FromStr` and `Default`. Equality and hashing read the code text.
- `from_code` refuses a bad code at the byte of the fault: an open quote or bracket, an unknown bracket, a colour past `[Color56]`, a condition that is not a number, a `\`/`_`/`*` with nothing after it, or a fifth section.
- `Rendered { text, color, fill: Option<(char, usize)>, shorter }`. `fill` is the character and its character offset (addendum 3).
- Rendering covers everything design 3.4 lists: General's 11-character rule after 15-digit rounding (with `shorter`), up to four sections with conditions and colours, all digit placeholders, thousands and scaling commas, percent, scientific and engineering notation, fractions, literals, `_x`, `*x`, `@`, `[$sym-locale]`, `[$-F800]`/`[$-F400]`, every date and time token including elapsed `[h] [m] [s]` and the 1900 leap-year bug, and half-away-from-zero rounding on the 15-digit form.
- It builds the text on the stack, so it allocates only the output.
- `NumberFormat::from_code` and `NumberFormat::builtin` are deleted. `FormatCode::kind` is now the one place that decides what a number under a code is.
- The built-in table and the undeclared-id display codes moved here from `styles.rs`.

**Theme (`excel/theme.rs`, new)**
- `Theme` has `OFFICE` (the Office 2013+ colours), `scheme`, and `color(index)`, which swaps 0↔1 and 2↔3.
- `Workbook::theme()` reads the part the theme relationship names, once, or answers the default.
- `StyleSheet::resolve(&Color, &Theme)` handles rgb, theme and indexed colours (the file's palette, else the default one) with ECMA-376 §18.8.19 tint on HLS. It answers `None` for auto and for indexed 64/65.

**Styles (`style.rs`, `styles.rs`, `workbook.rs`, `sheet.rs`)**
- New types: `StylePatch` (clearable fields as `Option<Option<_>>`, and `decimals` per addendum 5), `Borders` and `BorderPreset` (addendum spellings).
- New methods: `Workbook::cell_style`, `Workbook::set_style` and `StyleSheet::format`.
- `set_style` checks the patch before touching anything. It derives each distinct (source style, border edges) pair once, and rolls the styles table back if anything fails.
- Whole rows and whole columns set the row or column style and patch only the cells present; a column span is split where needed. Any other range creates blank cells only where the style actually changes.
- Border presets follow the range: `Outside` draws only the outline.
- A code equal to a built-in's en-US code interns to the built-in id. The first fill interned pads the list to the reserved `[none, gray125]` (P1b open item).
- Changing a number format re-reads the cell's value through `DateSystem`.
- `rebase` now keeps styles appended after the package was built (P1b open item). The package carries the table it wrote; adopting it re-appends the newer styles and remaps any cell, row or column whose index the package's own temporal styles took. A test runs `set_style` between `into_package` and `rebase`.

**Typed entry (`excel/entry.rs`, new)**
- `Entry::from_text` implements every rule in the 3.5 table, plus durations past 24 hours and times with seconds or AM/PM.
- New workbook methods: `set_entry`, `entry_text` and `display_text`.
- A property test checks that typing a cell's `entry_text` back in leaves its value, style and formula unchanged, starting from five different formats.

**Pins**
- 288 (code, value, text) rows in `rust/tests/excel/format.rs`. 242 of them LibreOffice rendered identically through the `lo_recalc` harness; 24 more are cases where LibreOffice is known to differ and Excel is followed, each with its reason.
- Three allocation pins:
  - rendering under a parsed code allocates 0 when the text fits inline, 1 otherwise;
  - `display_text` allocates nothing per call, because the code is parsed once per style;
  - `set_style` over 10,000 cells in 3 styles interns exactly 3; 2,500 cells cost 15 allocations and 10,000 cost 17.
- One `iobase_calls` pin: a save after a patch writes the styles part instead of copying it.
- openpyxl now reads back bold, a solid fill, a border, a custom code, a built-in code and a date written through `set_entry`/`set_style`.

deviations: `Entry` has two variants the design does not list: `Quoted(Str)`, which is text typed after `'` and states quotePrefix, and `Error(ExcelError)`, for the 18 error spellings. The design's four variants have no way to say either, and `set_entry` would otherwise have to parse the text a second time.
Built-in id 47 now reads as `mm:ss.0` instead of the ECMA-376 `mmss.0`. Excel and Apache POI both use `mm:ss.0`, and LibreOffice renders id 47 with a colon.

Where LibreOffice and Excel are known to differ, Excel is followed, and each case is pinned with its reason. The cases:
- `-0.001` under `0.00` shows `-0.00`.
- `#.##` of 1 shows `1.`.
- General uses the 11-character rule; LibreOffice's CSV export writes every digit.
- Clocks are rounded to the unit they show; LibreOffice truncates.
- The 1900 system has a 29 February 1900, serial 0 is `1/0/1900` and serial 1 is `1/1/1900`.
- `am/pm` and `a/p` keep the case they are written in.
- `[$-F400]` is `h:mm:ss AM/PM`.
- A boolean shows `TRUE`/`FALSE` whatever the format.
- A negative serial or one past 9999-12-31 renders as empty text with fill `('#', 0)`.

Section choice with conditions follows LibreOffice, because no Excel source was available: the sign is dropped only for `[<0]`/`[<=0]` sections and for the else sections, and a section that shows no number shows no sign. `%%` scaling and `?` placeholders ahead of a thousands separator are left unpinned for the same reason.

Tint is exact ECMA-376 floating HLS with rounding. It matches Excel's gray palette exactly (F2F2F2, D9D9D9, BFBFBF, A6A6A6, 808080, 7F7F7F, 595959, 404040, 262626, 0D0D0D). Colored accents may differ from Excel's own palette by ±1–2 per channel, and published Excel values disagree among themselves (2F5597 vs 305496), so those are asserted only by direction.

The read path changed: a number under a date format that no day spells (for example -3) now reads as that number with General meaning instead of refusing the whole sheet. Without this, a workbook where `set_style` gave a negative number a date format could not be reopened. `DateSystem`'s own refusals are unchanged.
`set_style` refuses bounded ranges that would create more than 2,097,152 blank cells (a new safety bound, named in the refusal). Whole rows and whole columns are not limited.

Public additions beyond the design: `FormatCode::general`, `FormatCode::is_general`, `StyleSheet::format`, `Theme::OFFICE`, `Theme::scheme`, `Theme::color`, and the `vocabulary!` methods on `BorderPreset` (`ALL`, `as_str`, `from_attribute`, `Display`).

`StyleSheet` now tracks two counts: a baseline taken after reading (which includes the default entries padded in for index 0) and the appends made since. A save writes the held styles only when something was really appended, so a part that lacks `cellXfs` is still copied as stored.
`with_decimals` on General has no cell value to read, so it answers `0.0…` for a positive delta and `0` for a negative one, instead of Excel's count of the decimals currently displayed.
open: Benchmarks for rendering, `set_style` and `set_entry` are not added: `rust/benchmarks/` is outside this file set.

`.api-inventory.txt` and `.api-bindings.txt` (P12) need the new names:
- `excel::{format, theme, entry, FormatCode, Rendered, Theme, Entry, StylePatch, Borders, BorderPreset}`
- `FormatCode::{from_code, builtin, general, is_general, kind, render, with_decimals, code}`
- `Theme::{OFFICE, scheme, color}`
- `StyleSheet::{resolve, format}`
- `Workbook::{theme, cell_style, set_style, set_entry, entry_text, display_text}`
They must also drop `NumberFormat::{from_code, builtin}`. The stale `style_index` line reported by `check_api_inventory.py` predates this phase (P1b).
Docs and skills (`docs/media/index.md` Excel section, `skills/`) have no entries for the new surface yet (P12).
The Python and Node bindings are not updated (P10/P11). No binding called the deleted `NumberFormat::from_code`/`builtin`.

Merged ranges get no special treatment in `set_style`: every cell of the range is patched. Where a formatted row meets a formatted column, `set_style` on whole columns does not create cells, as the design says.
Uncomputed formulas entered through `set_entry` hold a null cached value until the P5 evaluator; the dirty save's `fullCalcOnLoad` asks Excel to compute them.
Not run: the whole-workspace suite, the `--all-features` lane (CI's job) and `cargo bench`.

side.summary:
I built the P3 side-agent UI work in `cli/assets/excel/`. All 18 modules pass `node --check`, the Node unit smoke passes 30 of 30, and the Playwright check against the dev server passes 71 of 71 with no console errors. Nothing was committed. No cargo, maturin or npm build ran, no .rs file was touched, and cargo fmt did not run.

**What was built**
- **`js/sheets.js`** (new; exports `Sheets`, `movePosition`, `dropBefore`). The tab strip moved here out of `main.js`, and the sheet commands out of `ribbon.js`.
  - Commands: `insertSheet`, `addSheet`, `deleteSheet` (asks to confirm), `renameSheet`, `moveSheet`, `hideSheet`, `unhideSheet`, `sheetsBack`, `sheetsForward`.
  - Double-click renames in place. Enter or leaving the field sends `renameSheet`; Escape keeps the old name. A name the service refuses stays in the field with the service's reason shown as a toast.
  - Dragging a tab shows a drop mark and sends `moveSheet {sheet, to}`. `to` counts hidden sheets. Escape cancels the drag.
  - The Move… dialog asks "before which sheet", or "(move to end)".
  - The arrows scroll the strip one tab at a time and show `aria-disabled` when there is nowhere to go; the mouse wheel also scrolls it.
  - Ctrl+PgUp/PgDn work from the grid and from a focused tab. `app.switchSheet` now calls `sheets.step`.
- **Fill handle.**
  - `geometry.js` gains `fillTarget(source, row, column)` and `Viewport.corner(range)`.
  - `grid.js`: pressing the handle starts a fill drag. The pointer shows `data-cursor="handle"`, the grid shows `data-fill` and `data-fill-target`, the view auto-scrolls, Escape cancels, and a double-click on the handle raises `filldouble`.
  - `render.js`: `paintFill` draws a grey dashed frame around the target, and shades the cells a drag back inside the selection would clear.
  - `ribbon.js`: the `fillHandle` command sends `fill` with `mode: series`, or `copy` when Ctrl is held at release. A drag back inside the selection sends a `clear` of contents. The `fillToRegion` command fills down to the bottom of the current region.
- **`dialogs.js`.**
  - `findReplace` (Ctrl+F, Ctrl+H, and the Find & Select menu):
    - Find Next asks `GET find` from the active cell and selects the match, switching sheets if needed.
    - Replace All sends the `replace` op and reports "All done. We made N replacements."
    - The Replace tab searches formulas only, and the dialog remembers the last search.
  - `sortDialog` (Custom Sort): a header toggle; columns named by the header's text; up to 64 levels, each with move up, move down and delete; OK sends one `sort` op. The range and header guess come from `sortTarget`, now exported from `ribbon.js` and also used by the A→Z/Z→A sort.
  - Format Cells: the Number tab's sample now comes from `GET format` (addendum 9), 120 ms after the last change. It shows the service's colour and its `*` fill; a code the service refuses shows its reason under the sample.
- **Copy marker (addendum 8).**
  - `markerOf` parses `{instance}:{generation}:{revision}:{key}:{range}`. A paste is our internal `paste` only when both instance and generation match; otherwise it is `pasteText`.
  - P2's localStorage workaround (`recordCopy`/`copiedHere`) is deleted, since the instance id closes the gap it covered.
  - `api.adopt` records `instance`, and a different instance starts over like a new generation.
  - `main.reloadWorkbook` reloads everything when the instance changes.
- **Contract addendum item 10** (`GET find`) is appended to the scratchpad `contract-addendum.md`.

**Scratch tooling**
- `devstore.py`: a UUIDv7 `instance`, the wildcard matcher, `code_error`, find, the `replace` op (every cell checked before any changes) and `format_preview`.
- `dev.py`: `GET find` and `GET format`, the export marker with the instance, and a `YGG_ASSETS` override so it can serve another copy of the UI.
- `check.js` gains 10 new steps and adjusts 3 older ones; `unit.mjs` gains 6 new tests (the marker test is rewritten); `repro-remove.js` is new.

deviations: Addendum 10 names the search text `text`, as the task listed it, while the `replace` op's body names the same fact `find`. That is two spellings of one fact; the foreground should pick one.

Addendum 10 replaces §8.3's find row: the parameters `q`, `after`, `case` and `whole` and the `{"match":…}` wrapper become `text`, `from`, `matchCase` and `entireCell`, and the answer is `{sheet, ref}` or `null`. Addendum defaults: `scope=sheet`, `in=values`. The UI always sends every parameter, with `in=formulas` as Excel's default.

Find and Replace offers Find Next and Replace All only. There is no one-cell Replace and no Find All, because the `replace` op has no cell or range scope and a client-side replace would reimplement the wildcard rule. Find searches the sheet or the workbook, never the selection, because the endpoint takes no range.
Find from a chart sheet: with the Sheet scope the dialog says to show a worksheet; with the Workbook scope it starts at the next visible worksheet and sends no `from`.
Fill handle: Ctrl at release sends `copy`, as §10 says. In Excel, Ctrl on a single number switches to a series instead; the service's series rule copies a lone number anyway.

Fill handle: dragging back inside the selection clears the contents it leaves behind (a `clear` op), as Excel does; §10 does not mention this. The axis is chosen by distance in cells, not pixels, with a tie going vertical. A double-click fills down to the bottom of the current region (§10), which approximates Excel's adjacent-column extent.

Code moved between modules: the tab strip left main.js and the sheet commands left ribbon.js for sheets.js (§10's file list). The menu labels 'Move or Copy…' / 'Move or Copy Sheet…' became 'Move…' / 'Move Sheet…', because §8.4 has no copy-sheet op.
The Move dialog lists the visible sheets plus '(move to end)'. The end, and a drag past the last tab, means the end of the full list, hidden sheets included.
A refused sheet name is shown as a toast with the field kept open, not as a modal error. Leaving the field commits, as Enter does.

Copy marker: P2's localStorage record of exported markers is deleted, replaced by comparing the instance id (addendum 8). A changed-cells check against the change feed still guards a marker from another tab of the same service.

Custom Sort: each level has its own move up, move down and delete buttons, instead of Excel's toolbar acting on a selected level. There is no Copy Level, Sort On or Options, since the `sort` op carries only a column and a direction per key. The order labels ('Smallest to Largest' or 'A to Z') are chosen from the first data cell's kind in the loaded tiles. Column lists are capped at 1024 columns.

Format Cells sample: it asks the service on open and after every change (120 ms debounce), and for any category, General and Text included. OK is not blocked when the preview was refused; the service's `setStyle` refusal then shows in the dialog as before.
A P2 browser step ('context menus…') now waits for a newly inserted sheet to load before deleting it, as the P2 'sheets' step already did. See the open race below.
open: Pre-existing race, not fixed and not caused by P4: deleting a sheet right after inserting it, before its first tiles and the formula-bar lookup have landed, makes the client ask for `tiles/*` and `cells/A1` of the removed sheet, which answer 404 with console errors. Reproduced with 17 x 404 against the committed pre-P4 UI: `LAT=60 NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers node $SCRATCH/ui/repro-remove.js 8`. It showed up once in the full check (1 of 5 runs, under CPU load). Proposed fix, in main.js and editor.js: before sending `removeSheet`, `applyEdit` waits for that sheet's pending show, its first frame's tiles and the editor's entry lookup.
Contract for the foreground: `text` (addendum 10) vs `find` (the `replace` op) — one spelling should win.
Service work: P8 must implement addendum 10 (`GET find`), 9 (`GET format`) and 8 (the `instance` field and marker). Only the dev server answers them so far.

Ctrl+F does nothing on a chart sheet: showing a chart sheet never focuses the grid mirror, so the keys stay on the tab (pre-existing P1/P2 behaviour). Find is still reachable from the ribbon's Find & Select menu, which the check exercises.

Not browser-tested: read-only mode for the fill handle, rename and move (each refuses with a toast; the fill handle still draws); touch drags of tabs (touch is ignored, a tap still switches); a service restart changing `instance` mid-session; browsers other than Chromium.
Not run, per instructions: cargo, maturin, npm builds, cargo fmt. Screenshots 34-42 are in $SCRATCH/ui/shots/.

findings.issue: `best_fraction` computes `p0 + k * p1` in u64 with no overflow guard. A fraction section with no integer placeholder (`??/??`, `???/???`, `#/###`) on a large number panics in debug and wraps in release. Confirmed by probe: `#/#(*100B2` and `???/???` on 1.2345678901234568e17 panic with 'attempt to multiply with overflow'. The same paths print `18446744073709551615/1` (u64::MAX) for 1e300 and inf. A fuzz run of 1.5M random codes hit this panic 1,772 times, always a `?/?` section, none elsewhere. A hostile workbook (cell 1e18 under `??/??`) can crash tile rendering. AGENTS: caller input never reaches a panic.
findings.fix: Use `checked_mul`/`checked_add` for the semiconvergent and fall back to `(p1, q1)` on overflow. In `write_fraction`, when `part` is at or above 2^53 or the numerator would exceed `u64`, take the same path as a value no fraction spells: the rounded integer over 1, or the `#` fill that `render_date` uses. Pin `??/??` at 1e17, 1e18 and 1.8e19 in rust/tests/excel/format.rs, and NaN/inf under a fraction.

findings.issue: `number_shape` counts placeholders in `u16` (`integer += 1` at 2512, `fraction += 1` at 2508). `FormatCode::from_code` therefore panics (debug) or wraps (release) on a section with more than 65,535 placeholders. Confirmed by probe: 200,000 `0`, `0.` plus 200,000 `0`, and `#,` repeated 100,000 times each panic in `from_code`. It is reachable on open from an untrusted styles.xml: `StyleSheet::read` calls `FormatCode::from_file`, which calls `from_code`. `from_code` has no length bound, so render output and `with_decimals` work are unbounded too (1 MB text, 100k-token sections). Excel itself limits a format code to 255 characters.
findings.fix: In `FormatCode::from_code`, refuse a code over 255 characters with `Error::Parse` at byte 255, reason 'expected at most 255 characters'. `from_file` already turns a refusal into General, so an oversize file code is safe. Add tests with 300 zeros and 200,000 zeros. Optionally also use `saturating_add`/`u32` for the `integer`, `fraction` and `scale` counters.

findings.issue: `set_entry` ignores a Text-formatted cell. After `set_style` with `@`, typing `007` stores Float64(7.0), `1/2/2024` stores the serial 45293, and `=1+1` becomes a formula (all confirmed by probe). In Excel, entries into a Text-format cell stay text and formulas are not evaluated; that is how users keep leading zeros and IDs, and the ribbon offers it (addendum 5: `@` is built-in 49). The design says the value is 'what the cell's format then reads it as', and the Text format reads it as text. `typing_a_cell_s_entry_text_again_leaves_the_cell_as_it_is` includes `Some("@")` as a start format, but it only proves self-consistency, not this.
findings.fix: Add `FormatCode::is_text()` (first section is `Shape::Text`). In `set_entry`, when the cell's current format is text and the entry is not `Blank`, store `Scalar::from(text)` verbatim (no number/date/formula/error/quote reading, and a leading `'` may be left as typed) with the cell's style unchanged. Pin `007`, `1/2/2024` and `=1+1` under `@`.

findings.issue: A lone `-` or `+` (also `--` and `- `) reaches `Formula::from_entry` and is refused with 'expected an operand at the end'. The design table sends `+` or `-` to a formula only when a non-number follows, and Excel keeps a lone `-` as text; it is the usual dash placeholder. Confirmed by probe. The editor would reject and revert that entry, and AGENTS says the intent is unambiguous.
findings.fix: For a text starting with `+` or `-`, fall back to `Entry::Text` when `Formula::from_entry` fails because nothing follows the leading sign(s) (text that is only sign characters and spaces). Keep the error for `-*` and the other malformed formulas. Add `-`, `+` and `--` to the text cases in rust/tests/excel/entry.rs.

findings.issue: `set_entry` is not atomic. It interns the wanted style (line 921) before `Cell::from_scalar(...)?` (line 941) and `insert_cell` can refuse. A 40,000-character `'xxx…` entry returns the 32,767-character error yet leaves the styles table grown from 1 to 2 (confirmed by probe). `is_appended()` then makes the next save rewrite the styles part with an unused xf. `set_style` does this correctly with checkpoint/rollback; AGENTS says mutations fail atomically.
findings.fix: Build and validate the cell (text length, grid) before interning, or wrap the interning in `table.checkpoint()` / `rollback()` as `set_style` does. Pin that a refused `set_entry` leaves `style_sheet().len()` unchanged.

findings.issue: `Theme::from_xml` does not stop after the first `a:clrScheme`. `in_scheme` is set again by any later `a:clrScheme`, such as those inside `a:extraClrSchemeLst/a:extraClrScheme`, and their slots overwrite the workbook's real scheme. Theme parts that carry extra schemes then resolve every theme colour wrongly.
findings.fix: Stop reading (break the loop) at the first `</a:clrScheme>` after a scheme was entered, or track that a scheme was already read. Add a test with an `extraClrSchemeLst` holding a different scheme.

findings.issue: One owner per fact: this phase adds two more private copies of the civil-date algorithm (`from_days` here, `days_from_civil` at rust/src/excel/entry.rs:379). The crate already owns it in `crate::timezone::{civil_from_days, days_from_civil}`, which `temporal.rs`, `zip/format.rs`, `fix/entry.rs` and `http/cookie.rs` call. entry.rs also re-derives leap years and month lengths instead of validating by round trip, as `temporal.rs` does.
findings.fix: Delete both copies. Call `crate::timezone::civil_from_days` and `days_from_civil` (Excel's years, 1900 to 9999, fit i32/u32). In `entry::date`, validate with `civil_from_days(days_from_civil(y, m, d)) == (y, m, d)` and drop the leap-year table.

findings.issue: Owner split. `Entry::from_text` (the forward reading) is in entry.rs, but its inverse `entry_text`, the number spelling `entry_number`, and the clock/day writers are free helpers in format.rs, so one grammar has two owners. Design 3.1 gives entry.rs 'user text to a cell', and AGENTS says a value's behavior is a method on it. Separately, `DEFAULT_PALETTE` (line 129) is colour vocabulary owned in format.rs while `StyleSheet::resolve` reads it, so the default palette has no colour-module owner. `[ColorN]` sections render from the default palette even when the styles part replaces `indexedColors`, while `StyleSheet::resolve` honours the part's palette: two answers for one fact.
findings.fix: Move `entry_text` into entry.rs as an `Entry` associated fn (e.g. `Entry::spell(value, percent, quoted, system)`), making only `entry_number` `pub(crate)` in format.rs. Move `DEFAULT_PALETTE` to theme.rs. Either document that `Rendered::color` for `[ColorN]` is the default palette or resolve it through `StyleSheet`.

findings.issue: The safety bound counts the area of every bounded range, but the `set_style` docs (and the deviation report) say it refuses ranges 'putting more than 2,097,152 blank cells'. A used range of 2.5M existing cells (50 columns by 50,000 rows), bolded with Ctrl+B, is refused although it creates no blank cell.
findings.fix: Count only the cells that would be created (area minus present cells, via the sheet), or reword the doc and the refusal to say every cell of a bounded range counts. Pin whichever is chosen.

findings.issue: Dead second clauses in the `Patcher::plan` conditions. Line 2463: `own.is_some_and(|own| own != derived)` is already `derived != source`, because `source == own` when `own` is Some. Lines 2477 and 2503: `row_style(row).is_none() && derived != DEFAULT` and `style.is_none() && derived != DEFAULT` are already `derived != source`, because `source` is DEFAULT when the style is None. AGENTS: delete dead branches you touch.
findings.fix: Reduce each condition to `derived != source`.

findings.issue: Cost pins the design promises are missing. Design 12.2 says open plus `parse_all` reads 'sst, styles and theme once', but nothing pins `Workbook::theme()` (a member read on first use, 0 for a workbook with no theme part, none on the second call). AGENTS also requires a benchmark for each surface touched; `rust/benchmarks/media/excel.rs` has no row for `FormatCode::render`, `set_style` or `set_entry`. The implementer reported the benchmark gap; the theme pin is not reported.
findings.fix: Add an `excel` iobase_calls test: `theme()` twice equals one member read, and zero reads without a theme relationship. Assign the render, `set_style` and `set_entry` benchmark rows to the next phase that owns rust/benchmarks/media/excel.rs (P4/P5), and record it in the handoff.

findings.issue: FormatCode::with_decimals panics on a code the reader could not parse. from_file() (l.527) stores the raw code text but shares General's sections, whose span is (0,7) and decimals Decimals::General(0,7). with_decimals then slices &self.code[0..7] (l.643). Reproduced: an xlsx with numFmt '[Foo]0' (also '0.00"x', '0;0;0;0;0') and set_style(decimals: Some(1)) on that cell panics with 'byte index 7 is out of bounds of `[Foo]0`'. A raw code longer than 7 bytes gets garbage or a char-boundary panic. Reachable from any file plus the ribbon's decimal buttons (a Decimals patch reads the source style's from_file code). The test that covers unreadable file codes (a_file_code_this_reader_refuses...) never calls with_decimals.
findings.fix: Give the from_file fallback its own single General section with span (0, code.len()) and decimals: None, so with_decimals returns self unchanged. Also slice with self.code.get(span.0..span.1) and return self on None. Add a test: open a file whose numFmt is '[hm]yyyy' or '[Foo]0', run set_style with decimals +1 and -1, and assert the cell is unchanged and nothing panics.

findings.issue: from_code has no length bound, and number_shape counts placeholders in u16 with plain '+=': denominator_digits (l.2452), scale (l.2486), fraction (l.2508), integer (l.2512). Reproduced: from_code('0.'+'0'*70000), '0'*70000, '0'+','*70000 and '0/'+'0'*70000 each panic with 'attempt to add with overflow' (debug and test builds; silent wrap in release). Reachable from a file numFmt via from_file, and from StylePatch.check() through the service's numberFormat, so a 400 becomes a panic. SectionBuilder::literal also rebuilds its SmolStr on every character, so long literal runs are quadratic.
findings.fix: Refuse a code longer than 255 characters in FormatCode::from_code with Error::Parse at the byte of the 256th character. Excel's own limit is 255, and from_file then falls back to General. Use saturating_add on the u16 counters as a second guard. Add tests for 256-character codes and for the four 70,000-placeholder shapes.

findings.issue: set_style silently changes the type of a temporal cell whose style is General. Cells built with Sheet::set_cell(Scalar::date32) or the record writer have StyleId::DEFAULT and format Date, and the save writes them under an interned yyyy-mm-dd style (sheet.rs:1950). Reproduced: A1=date32(19724), set_style(bold) gives A1 = Float64(45293.0) with display '45293', and the saved file holds a bold serial number; an untouched B1 still saves as a date. Cause: Patcher::derive starts from the General style, then Sheet::restyle passes table.number_format(new style) = General and Cell::restyle (cell.rs:1152) turns the date into its serial. Fixing only the value is not enough: the writer replaces the cell's whole style with the default temporal style whenever format is temporal and the xf does not classify as it, so a bolded date would lose the bold at save. Related: cell_style, display_text and set_entry judge such a cell as General while the saved file shows a date.
findings.fix: In Patcher::plan, for a present cell whose format() is temporal while table.number_format(cell.style()) != cell.format(), take as the source the interned style 'own style with number_format = the temporal code' (the code Splice::temporal uses, kept in one place). Then bold keeps the date and the written xf carries the bold. Only re-read the value in Cell::restyle when the patch states number_format or decimals. Give display_text and cell_style the same effective format. Add a test: date32 via set_cell, set_style(bold), assert the value is still Date32, it saves and reopens as a bold date, and cell_style.number_format is 'yyyy-mm-dd'.

findings.issue: Entry::from_text and Workbook::entry_text are not inverse, and a lone sign errors. (a) A lone '+' or '-' (ledger dash) goes to Formula::from_entry and set_entry('-') fails with Parse 'expected an operand at the end'; '--' and '- ' fail too. Excel stores a lone '-' or '+' as text. (b) entry_text returns a string cell's text unchanged even when it would read as something else, so opening the editor on such a cell and committing changes it. Reproduced with cells from set_cell: 'TRUE' -> Boolean, '007' -> 7, '=A1' -> formula, '1/2/2024' -> date, '#N/A' -> error, '-5' -> number, and a text cell '-' whose entry text '-' cannot be retyped at all. The property test only starts from typed texts, which carry quotePrefix, so it never sees these cells.
findings.fix: In from_text, treat '+' or '-' followed only by whitespace as Entry::Text. In entry_text, prefix a string cell with '\'' whenever Entry::from_text(text) is not Entry::Text(text) (or the text starts with '\''). Add set_cell(Scalar::from(text)) starts, including 'TRUE', '007', '=A1', '1/2/2024', '#N/A', '-5' and '-', to typing_a_cell_s_entry_text_again_leaves_the_cell_as_it_is.

findings.issue: set_entry is not atomic. It interns the wanted style (table.intern at l.918-921) before Cell::from_scalar / insert_cell can fail. Reproduced: set_entry of "'" plus 40,000 characters returns InvalidRecord (over 32,767) but leaves a new quotePrefix xf (style count 1 -> 2), and the workbook is dirty and rewrites styles.xml on the next save. The same happens for a too-long plain text typed into a quotePrefix cell.
findings.fix: Build the Cell (Cell::from_scalar, formula, error) first and intern the style last. Or take table.checkpoint() before the intern and table.rollback(&checkpoint) on any later error, as set_style does. Test that a refused set_entry leaves style_sheet().len() and is_dirty() unchanged.

findings.issue: set_style loses edges when ranges in one call overlap. Patcher::plan derives every range's style from the sheet's original style, and the later push in plan.cells overwrites the earlier one. Reproduced: ranges ['A1:B2','B2:C3'] with BorderPreset::Outside leave B2 with left and top only, while two sequential calls give all four edges. Excel applies a multi-area selection cumulatively. The same shape would apply a 'decimals' delta once per range if made cumulative instead.
findings.fix: Combine per cell before deriving: OR the border edge masks (and the other range-independent facts) of every range that contains the cell, and derive once per (source, mask). Alternatively derive later ranges from the planned style, keeping decimals single-shot. Add a test with overlapping Outside ranges.

findings.issue: Theme::from_xml keeps parsing after the first </a:clrScheme>, so a theme with <a:extraClrSchemeLst><a:extraClrScheme><a:clrScheme> overrides the workbook's real colours. Reproduced: a theme1.xml with an extra scheme (accent1 ABCDEF, lt1 EEEEEE) makes Workbook::theme() answer accent1 = ABCDEF and lt1 = EEEEEE instead of the main scheme's colours. Also, an empty slot element (<a:dk1/>) never clears 'slot', so the next slot's children are assigned to the previous one.
findings.fix: Stop reading at the first Event::End of clrScheme (break out of the loop). Clear 'slot' on an Event::Empty slot element. Add a test with an extraClrSchemeLst carrying different colours.

findings.issue: set_entry ignores a Text-formatted cell. In a cell formatted '@' (numFmtId 49), Excel keeps whatever is typed as text, formulas included. Reproduced: after set_style(number_format '@'), set_entry '007' gives Float64(7.0), '=1+1' gives an uncomputed formula and '1/2/2024' gives Float64(45293). Leading-zero ids and phone numbers in Text-formatted columns are corrupted, and the round-trip test lists Some("@") as a start format, so it pins this behaviour.
findings.fix: In set_entry, when table.format(source) is a text-only code (first section Shape::Text, i.e. '@'), map every non-empty entry except Entry::Quoted to Entry::Text(text) (keep Blank for ''). Add tests for '007', '=1+1' and 'TRUE' typed into a '@' cell.

findings.issue: Entry keeps more than the 15 significant digits that entry_text spells, and the property test hides it. from_text('12345678901234567') stores 1.2345678901234568e16; entry_text answers '1.23456789012346E+17'-style 15-digit text, so typing it back changes the value. The test skips any first value with !fifteen(number), and entry_text_spells_each_value expects '1.23456789012346E+17' for a typed 18-digit number without asserting the round trip. Separately, a datetime typed with seconds ('1/2/2024 10:30:15') is suggested m/d/yyyy h:mm, so the typed seconds are stored but not displayed (temporal() drops clock()'s format for the datetime branch).
findings.fix: Quantise a typed number to the 15-digit form entry_number uses (for example value = entry_number(value, false).parse()) before storing it. Remove the fifteen() skip, or restrict it to cells read from a file. For the datetime branch use the clock's format: 'm/d/yyyy h:mm:ss' when seconds are typed.

findings.issue: adopt_styles (used by rebase) swallows an intern failure: 'if let Ok(to) = table.intern(style)' skips the style when the table is full, so no id is moved. A cell, row or column that named that appended style then silently names whatever the package put at that index (for example a temporal style). It is only reachable at the 64,000 cell-format limit, but it is silent corruption.
findings.fix: Propagate the error from adopt_styles and have rebase return it before committing any other state. Or move the not-mapped cells, rows and columns to StyleId::DEFAULT explicitly.

fixed.summary:
I fixed all 20 findings except one part of F19, which I left as it is on purpose. Fifteen are distinct; five repeat another: F13 repeats F2, F15 repeats F5, F17 repeats F6, F18 repeats F3, and F14a sits beside F14b. All smoke checks pass, and each fix has a test.

- **F1 (fixed):** fraction rendering can no longer overflow. The numerator is a double: from 2^53 on, a value is itself over 1, and every u64 step is checked. An infinite or not-a-number value renders `#NUM!` under any format. Pinned `??/??` at 1e17, 1e18, 1.8e19 and 1e300, plus `?/8`, `# ?/?`, and NaN/inf.
- **F2/F13 (fixed):** `FormatCode::from_code` refuses a code of 256 or more characters, at the byte of the 256th. The placeholder counters also saturate. Pinned with 256 and 300 zeros, 200,000 zeros, the three 70,000-character shapes and `#,`×100,000.
- **F12 (fixed):** a file code this reader refuses now gets its own General section with no decimals, so the ribbon's decimal buttons leave it unchanged. `with_decimals` also slices with `get`. Pinned `[hm]yyyy`, `[Foo]0`, `0.00"x`, a five-section code and a 302-character code at ±1 and ±15.
- **F3/F18 (fixed):** in a cell formatted as text (`@`), whatever is typed stays text, including a formula that would not read. A `'` still sets `quotePrefix`. This goes through the new crate-private `Entry::from_text_in`.
- **F4 and F14b (fixed):**
  - An entry made only of signs (`-`, `+`, `--`) is text.
  - `entry_text` now puts a `'` before any text that would read back as something else.
  - A new test puts cells by value (for example `TRUE`, `007`, `=A1`, dates, durations) and types their entry text back.
- **F5/F15 (fixed):** `set_entry` takes a style checkpoint and rolls it back on any refusal.
- **F6/F17 (fixed):** the theme reader stops at the first `</a:clrScheme>`, so extra schemes are ignored. An empty slot element no longer takes the next slot's colour.
- **F7 (fixed):** both copies of the date algorithm are gone. Code now calls `crate::timezone::civil_from_days` and `days_from_civil`, and `entry::date` checks a date by round trip.
- **F8 (fixed):**
  - `entry_text`'s body moved into `entry.rs` as `Entry::spell`.
  - `DEFAULT_PALETTE` moved to `theme.rs`, with one `indexed()` reader that `StyleSheet::resolve` and `[ColorN]` both use.
  - `display_text` renders through the new crate-private `render_in` with the file's palette. `FormatCode::render` documents that alone it uses the default palette.
- **F9 (fixed):** the `set_style` bound counts only blank cells created (area minus cells present), pinned at "got 2599999".
- **F10 (fixed):** the dead clauses went away when the planner was rewritten.
- **F11 (partly fixed):** a new pin shows `theme()` reads one member once, and nothing when the workbook has no theme part. The render, `set_style` and `set_entry` benchmark rows are passed to P4/P5 (see Open).
- **F14a (fixed):** a date, time or duration whose style does not read as one is now shown, patched and saved with its own style plus the crate's code for it (`yyyy-mm-dd` for a date). `StyleSheet::shown_style`/`shown_format`/`overrides` are used by `cell_style`, `display_text`, `entry_text`, `set_entry` and the style planner. The save now keeps the cell's own style: new `Splice::written`, so a bold date stays bold.
- **F16 (fixed):** when a call's ranges overlap, each cell, row and column is patched once, with every border edge each range draws on it. Decimals are added once.
- **F19 (partly fixed):** typed numbers keep 15 significant digits and the rest become zeros, as Excel does (KB 269370). Entry text spells numbers in full below 10^20. The test's 15-digit skip now applies only to temporals typed under a number format. The datetime-with-seconds format is unchanged (see Deviations).
- **F20 (fixed):** `rebase` works out the adopted styles first and returns the styles' refusal before changing anything. Pinned at the 64,000-format limit.

deviations: F19, datetime with seconds: not changed. Typing `1/2/2024 10:30:15` still suggests built-in 22 (`m/d/yyyy h:mm`). As far as I know, en-US Excel applies built-in 22 to any typed date and time: seconds are kept in the value but not shown, and a typed PM time shows in 24-hour form. I have not verified this against Excel itself.

F19, typed numbers: digits past the 15th significant one are truncated to zeros (Excel's documented rule, KB 269370). The reviewer suggested rounding through `entry_number`. With truncation, `4111111111111119` becomes 4111111111111110.

`entry_number` now spells numbers in full up to 20 integer digits (it was 15). A scientific spelling typed back into a General cell would suggest `0.00E+00`, and Excel's formula bar shows 16- to 20-digit numbers with their trailing zeros. One existing expectation changed: `123456789012345678` now spells `123456789012345000`.

F14b round trip: a string cell whose text would read as something else (`TRUE`, `007`, `=A1`) is spelled after a `'`. Typing that back keeps the value but sets `quotePrefix`, as a typed `'` always does. A number or boolean in a cell formatted `@` reads back as text, as in Excel. Both are stated in the `entry_text` doc, and the test checks value plus style with `quote_prefix` allowed to change.

F14a, beyond the finding: the sheet writer now saves a temporal cell with its own style plus the temporal code (new `Splice::written`), not the default style plus the code. A hand-built bold date cell therefore stays bold after a save. The record writer still uses `TemporalStyles`, which is keyed by format.

F14a side effect: clearing (`set_entry` with empty text) a date cell built in memory leaves a blank cell in the date style it showed, as clearing that saved file's cell in Excel would. Before, the cell was removed.

F16: for more than one range, the cells, rows and columns are gathered into BTreeMaps and patched in sheet order. A single range keeps the old single pass, so the 10,000-cell pin interns the same 3 styles. Columns are now always planned per column over `column_runs`, instead of pieces cut at the range edges; the result is the same.

New crate-private items: `FormatCode::render_in`, `FormatCode::is_text`, `Entry::from_text_in`, `Entry::spell`, `StyleSheet::overrides`, `shown_style`, `shown_format`, `Splice::written`, `theme::indexed`, and a static `temporal_format` in styles.rs. No public name was added or removed, so the inventories are unchanged by this round.
F13: `SectionBuilder::literal` still rebuilds its text per character. The 255-character bound limits that to at most 255² operations per code, so I did not rewrite it.
The F20 test builds a styles part of 63,999 formats and takes about 3 s in a debug build.
open: F11: benchmark rows for `FormatCode::render`, `Workbook::set_style` and `Workbook::set_entry` in rust/benchmarks/media/excel.rs are passed to the next phase that owns that file (P4/P5). Only the `theme()` cost pin was added here.

Not run: the whole workspace suite, the `--all-features` lane, `cargo bench`, and the Python and Node bindings (still broken since P1a/P1b; nothing in this round changed a public signature they call).

Docs and skills still have no entries for the P3 surfaces (P12). The docs should state the round-trip exceptions in the `entry_text` doc: `'` typed back sets `quotePrefix`, and numbers or booleans in `@` cells read back as text.
